name: Major cyber incidents
summary: Attacks on internet-exposed refrigeration controls hit supermarkets in several European countries
state: Attackers altered internet-exposed refrigeration controls at supermarkets in Belgium, the Netherlands, Ireland, Sweden, Portugal, Italy and other countries overnight into 2 Nov, forcing some stores to discard food; Belgium's federal prosecutor opened an investigation and no group has claimed it (The Hacker News; BleepingComputer). No national-scale outage of power, health or finance systems had been reported as of 7 Nov.
for_you: Businesses using internet-connected building controls should follow NCSC guidance on changing default passwords and patching.
rubric_hit: Attack disrupting large companies across countries = Watch

sources.title: The Hacker News — New wave of refrigeration cyberattacks hits supermarkets across Europe

why: Ransomware and state hacking now shut down hospitals, retailers, carmakers and airports for weeks.

rubric.alert: National-scale attack on critical infrastructure (power, health, finance), or a destructive state-attributed attack.
rubric.watch: Ransomware or attack disrupting a large company or critical service, or a mass-exploited zero-day.
rubric.normal: No major incidents disrupting critical services this week.
